scheme.label: Cascaded speed and current control (servo)
scheme.about: A speed regulator asks a torque, a current regulator in the rotor's frame makes it: the usual field-oriented servo, sampled once a carrier period with one period of computation.

sources.slew: the acceleration the torque limit gives the inertia with no load
sources.jerk: that acceleration reached in one time constant of the speed loop

sources.kp: symmetric optimum a decade below the current loop (ωs/2π = 100 Hz, a = 6.8): Kp = J·ωs, J = 0.00558 kg·m².
sources.ki: symmetric optimum a decade below the current loop (ωs/2π = 100 Hz, a = 6.8): Ki = Kp·ωs/a
sources.limit: the torque of the drive's current limit
the torque of the drive's current limit
sources.rate: the whole torque limit in half the speed loop's time constant, 1/(2·ωs)
sources.jerk: that rate reached in a quarter of the speed loop's time constant

sources.voltage_share: the share of the ideal voltage the stage gives at the design point (dead time, shortest pulse and the devices' drop), as the loss engine takes it

sources.kp_d: pole-zero cancellation at ωc/2π = 1,000 Hz (a twentieth of the 20,000 Hz sampling rate): Kp = ωc·Ld
sources.ki_d: pole-zero cancellation at ωc/2π = 1,000 Hz (a twentieth of the 20,000 Hz sampling rate): Ki = ωc·Rs
sources.kp_q: pole-zero cancellation at ωc/2π = 1,000 Hz (a twentieth of the 20,000 Hz sampling rate): Kp = ωc·Lq
sources.ki_q: pole-zero cancellation at ωc/2π = 1,000 Hz (a twentieth of the 20,000 Hz sampling rate): Ki = ωc·Rs

sources.advance: the delay around the loop in sampling periods: half the hold, and the computation

taken: no inertia is given: 0.00558 kg·m² is taken, which the torque limit runs up to the design speed in a quarter of a second
no load is given: one whose torque grows with the speed and asks the design torque at the design speed is taken

notes: control run: the simulated stretch is taken to repeat without end for the losses and settled temperatures
switching loss: estimated from gate and output charge, not from measured energy; gate charge at threshold not tabulated; taken as gate-source charge times threshold voltage over plateau voltage
output charge: scaled as the square root of voltage from 50 V to 48 V

recovery charge: above the 50 A it was measured at it is taken to grow as the square root of the current; it is taken as tabulated at 25 °C and 1.26 times that at 62 °C, the usual rise of a silicon junction; a datasheet's own hot figure is not read
reverse conduction: built from table points up to 100 A; reverse voltage taken as constant at its one tabulated point; it rises with current, so dead-time loss is underestimated
reverse conduction: only characterised at 25 °C, used at 62 °C
assumptions: case-to-heatsink resistance computed for a TO-220 on grease: 0.40 K/W (0.16 to 0.80)

no transient thermal data: the temperature swing within the period uses the response computed for a generic TO-220; the top of the range takes the junction to follow the loss at once, which no response can exceed
